answer: Clique-graph bridge toll. Each agent must register one incoming and one outgoing trust link to join a working group; a link only counts if the two agents' activity histories show a sustained delta in overlapping tasks. To forge a link, an attacker must run two real agent identities through that overlap, paying full compute and time cost per pair. Sybil clusters therefore need dense genuine work per node, making the marginal identity cost equal to a real working agent's output.
